extDescription.message: Your own list of redirects: open a URL and land straight on the page you actually need.

hint.message: When you open a URL from the “From” column, the browser goes straight to the “To” URL. Rules higher in the list take precedence. If a site redirects you by itself (e.g. to /welcome), add a rule for that page too.

permissionHint.message: When you save, Chrome will ask for access to the sites in the “From” column — redirects cannot work without it. The extension never reads page content or sends anything anywhere.

emptyState.message: No rules yet. Click “Add rule”, or open a site and click the extension icon.

typesExact.message: Exact URL — same domain and path; a trailing slash and anything after ? are ignored. https://example.com matches https://example.com/?a=1 but not /app.

typesDomain.message: Whole site — any page on this domain.

typesPrefix.message: Starts with — the URL starts with the given one (http and https are treated the same).

typesRegex.message: Regular expression — RE2 syntax; use groups \1, \2… in “To”. Example: ^https://old\.example\.com/(.*) → https://new.example.com/\1. Requires access to all sites.

fixErrors.message: Fix the errors in the highlighted rules

permissionDenied.message: Not saved: redirects cannot work without access to the sites

noAccess.message: Site access not granted yet — Chrome will ask for it when you save

regexUnsupported.message: Chrome does not support this expression: $1

errScheme.message: only http and https are supported

errLoop.message: The target URL matches this same rule — that would be an endless redirect

badgeNoAccess.message: Rules without site access: $1. Open the list and click “Save”.

popupNoAccess.message: Not working without site access: $1. Open “All rules” and click “Save”.

errQuota.message: Not saved: the rules take $1 KB, but Chrome sync holds about $2 KB. Delete some rules or shorten the regular expressions.

errRuleTooLong.message: The rule is too long: “From” and “To” together must fit in $1 KB

errTooManyRules.message: Not saved: $1 rules are enabled, but Chrome allows an extension at most $2. Delete or disable some rules.

noAccessWhy.message: This happens with imported rules, after syncing to another computer (Chrome grants access on each device separately), or if you clicked “Deny” in Chrome’s prompt.

accessIntro.message: Chrome will now show a prompt asking to “Read and change your data” on:

accessAllSites.message: all sites — required for regular-expression rules

accessWhy.message: That is how Chrome words any site access: without it the extension cannot redirect from these addresses. The extension never reads pages or sends anything anywhere — Chrome performs the redirect itself, and the access is used only for that. Once no rules need a site, the access is released.

importTitle.message: These addresses are already in your list

importIntro.message: Checked rules will be replaced with the version from the file; unchecked ones stay as they are. Exact copies are skipped automatically.
